title: Installation
description: Install sevDesk.NET and configure your project.
searchText: NuGet Package Install the sevDesk.NET package via the .NET CLI: Or via the NuGet Package Manager: Requirements - .NET 10.0 or later - A sevDesk account with an API token Project Setup Add the sevDesk.NET namespace to your project: Next Steps - Quick Start — Make your first API call - Configuration — Customize the client behavior - Authentication — Learn about API token management

title: Quick Start
description: Register services and make your first sevDesk API call.
searchText: Register Services In your Program.cs or startup configuration, register sevDesk.NET with dependency injection: This registers ISevDeskClient and all sub-clients with the DI container, including the HTTP client with authentication. Inject and Use Inject ISevDeskClient anywhere in your application: Available Clients ISevDeskClient provides access to 20 typed sub-clients: | Property | Interface | Description | |---|---|---| | Contacts | IContactClient | Manage customers, suppliers, and partners | |

title: Configuration
description: Configure SevDeskOptions for API token, base URL, and more.
searchText: SevDeskOptions The SevDeskOptions class controls how sevDesk.NET connects to the API: Configuration Properties | Property | Type | Required | Default | Description | |---|---|---|---|---| | ApiToken | string | Yes | — | Your 32-character sevDesk API token | | CustomBaseUrl | string? | No | null | Custom base URL (must be HTTPS or localhost) | | BaseUrl | string | — | https://my.sevdesk.de/api/v1 | Resolved base URL (uses CustomBaseUrl if set) | Validation AddSevDesk validates your configuration

title: Authentication
description: How sevDesk.NET handles API token authentication.
searchText: API Token sevDesk uses a simple API token for authentication. You can find your token in the sevDesk web app under Settings > Users > API Token. The token is a 32-character hexadecimal string that looks like: How It Works sevDesk.NET uses a DelegatingHandler called SevDeskAuthHandler to automatically add the API token to every HTTP request: The handler is registered automatically when you call AddSevDesk(). title: Pagination
description: How to paginate through large result sets with PaginationParameters.
headings: Total is nullable, and null is not 0
searchText: PaginationParameters All ListAsync methods accept an optional PaginationParameters object: SevDeskListResponse List methods return a SevDeskListResponse<T> containing the items and total count: - Items — The page of results - Total — The total number of matching records (for calculating total pages), or null when the API did not report one Total is nullable, and null is not 0 Every ListAsync requests countAll=true, which is what makes the API send total at all — but it does not send it reliably

description: Overview of all model types and enums in sevDesk.NET.
